conflicts.fact: Dimensions and capacities of the Kericho containers (anchoring dataset) change between lessons
conflicts.versions: L1: height ≈30 cm, opening diameter ≈20 cm; cylinder ≈9.4 L, cone ≈3.1 L, frustum ≈6.5 L. L2: cone has r=21 cm (diameter 42 cm), h=42 cm, capacity ≈19.4 L, and the matching cylinder has the same r and h. L4/L5/L6/L8: height 30 cm, diameter 28 cm (r=14 cm), cylinder ≈18.47 L, cone ≈6.16 L. L6 cites the drum as ≈18.5 L 'established in Lesson 4'. So the same containers have three incompatible sets of dimensions and capacities.

conflicts.fact: Frustum bucket capacity relative to cone and cylinder, and its dimensions
conflicts.versions: L1: frustum ≈6.5 L, about double the cone's 3.1 L, with a 20 cm opening. L4/L8: frustum with R=14, r=9, h=30 holds about 2/3 of the cylinder (bar ≈2/3 of the cylinder bar), roughly 12.3 L from the formula, against cone ≈6.16 L and cylinder ≈18.47 L. The frustum values in L1 and L4 are incompatible with each other.

conflicts.fact: Which end of the frustum is the wide end / bucket orientation
conflicts.versions: L4: top radius R, bottom radius r (R larger), and the frustum is a large cone with a small cone removed from the bottom. L8: the 'wide bottom (radius R)' is kept and it narrows to r. L5: top radius 14 and bottom radius 9 (top wider). The wide end is described as bottom in L8 but top in L4/L5.

conflicts.fact: Cone orientation / capacity of the cone with the same opening
conflicts.versions: L1 depicts the cone with its apex down with a top opening diameter equal to the cylinder's. L8 says the cone 'tapers to a point'. In L2 the cone's matching dimensions (r=21, h=42) are a different cone from L4's. The cone derivation in L8 Q1 uses a diameter of 56 cm (r=28 cm), h=30 cm, which differs from every other cone dimension (r=14, h=30) used in the unit.

conflicts.fact: Pyramidal frustum bin dimensions and the 'geometric mean' wording
conflicts.versions: L5 predict phase uses bin top side 26 cm, bottom 18 cm, h 30 cm, while the main problem uses top 30, bottom 20, h 40. L5 also says the formula expresses the 'average of two base areas weighted by their geometric mean' and calls the term √(A₁A₂) the geometric mean, while L4 calls R, r, and their geometric mean the interplay of radii; the term Rr is described inconsistently.

conflicts.fact: Number of lessons and sequence structure
conflicts.versions: L5 says 'Lesson 5 of 8', consistent with L8. But L5 also relies on 'Sub-Strand 2.1' and a cumulative 'Similarity & Enlargement panel' never built in L1–4, while L6 says ORANGE notes go to 'Lesson 7 (model making and measurement)' consistent; the L5 panel reference conflicts with the models described in L1–4.
